query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q4 FY2026 growth drivers Blackwell inference networking

output.content:
**NVIDIA Data Center revenue reached a record $62.3 billion in Q4 FY2026** (quarter ended January 2026), increasing **22% sequentially** and **75% year over year**; total company revenue was $68.1 billion. [[1]]

**The principal growth driver was the sustained ramp of Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra systems.** NVIDIA said Data Center revenue grew by roughly $11 billion versus Q3, with Blackwell architecture demand broadening across cloud providers, hyperscalers, AI-model developers, enterprises and sovereign customers. [[2]] Grace Blackwell systems represented approximately **two-thirds of quarterly Data Center revenue**, while nearly **nine gigawatts** of Blackwell infrastructure had been deployed and consumed by major cloud and hyperscale customers. [[2]]

**Inference was central to the demand thesis, rather than only training.** Management characterized agentic AI as an inflection point and positioned Grace Blackwell with NVLink as an inference platform with an order-of-magnitude lower cost per token. [[3]] NVIDIA also cited Blackwell Ultra performance of up to **50x higher** and cost up to **35x lower** for agentic AI relative to Hopper, while selected inference providers reported up to a **10x reduction in AI costs** using open-source models on Blackwell. [[3]] These economics matter because higher token throughput and lower per-token cost can improve AI-service-provider monetization and support continued infrastructure deployment. [[2]]

**Networking was the second major incremental contributor.** Q4 Data Center networking revenue was **$11 billion**, more than **3.5x** its year-earlier level. [[2]] NVIDIA attributed the year-over-year networking increase primarily to **NVLink 72 scale-up switches**, and its FY2026 10-K said Data Center networking revenue grew **142%** on the NVLink compute-fabric ramp for GB200 and GB300 systems plus growth in Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms. [[2]] [[4]]

**Bottom line:** Q4 FY2026 Data Center growth reflected a platform sale—Blackwell/Blackwell Ultra compute systems, inference-driven customer ROI, and tightly coupled scale-up and scale-out networking—not simply stand-alone GPU shipments. [[4]]
